title: The Great Gildersleeve
paragraphs: A pioneering situation comedy following the pompous but good-hearted Throckmorton P. Gildersleeve as he raises his niece and nephew and becomes part of everyday life in the town of Summerfield.

NBC family/situation comedy spun off from Fibber McGee and Molly. GRH includes a May 1941 audition, the regular series, several partially dated AFRS/AFRTS items, and one April 1957 archive item after the documented NBC finale.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Harold Peary weekly era (August 31, 1941 to June 14, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Willard Waterman weekly era (September 6, 1950 to June 2, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], 15-minute strip era (September 26, 1954 to June 23, 1955) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Final weekly era (October 6, 1955 to March 21, 1957) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Walter Tetley (performer), Lillian Randolph (performer), Richard LeGrand (performer), Earle Ross (performer), [[person|hal-peary|Hal Peary]] (performer), Jack Meakin (music, composer, and performer), and Andy White (writer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].
The stories often return to Youth, school, and parenting, Small-town civic life, Romance and courtship, Family and household life, Holiday episodes, and Money and household economics.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Radio spin-off and family-sitcom development and Network radio comedy during the television transition.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]], and [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]].
